Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70527
Published: 2026-Oct-04
PMID: 42830481



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2020, the World Health Organization (WHO) Collaborating Centre for Oral Cancer convened an international expert workshop to establish an updated consensus on the nomenclature and classification of oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs). The working group has defined OPMD as "any oral mucosal abnormality that is associated with a statistically increased risk of developing oral cancer", including leukoplakia, proliferative verrucous leukoplakia, erythroplakia, oral submucous fibrosis, oral lichen planus, actinic keratosis/actinic cheilitis, palatal lesions in reverse smokers, oral lupus erythematosus, dyskeratosis congenita, oral lichenoid lesions, and oral graft-versus-host disease. METHODS: A literature search was conducted to identify the available evidence on the malignant transformation of OPMDs. Systematic reviews with meta-analyses quantifying malignant transformation risks were selected and critically analyzed through narrative synthesis. RESULTS: Based on the available evidence, the malignant transformation risk is 6.64% (95% CI = 5.21-8.21) for oral leukoplakia, 1.40% (95% CI = 1.07-1.76) for oral lichen planus, 1.38% (95% CI = 0.16-3.38) for oral lichenoid lesions, 43.87% (95% CI = 31.93-56.13) for proliferative verrucous leukoplakia, and 6.00% (95% CI = 2.00-10.00) for oral submucous fibrosis. CONCLUSIONS: This narrative review presents the current evidence-based knowledge regarding the malignant transformation risks of the different OPMDs, with the aim of fulfilling the mission of the 3rd Global Oral Cancer Forum.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to systematically identify and annotate oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) genetic risk, construct OPC risk prediction models, and identify candidate drug targets for OPC treatment. METHODS: The OPC genome-wide association study was conducted in the UK Biobank involving 208 OPC patients and 328,248 healthy individuals. Functional annotations were performed using the FUMA website and the Sclinker statistical framework. OPC risk prediction models were constructed using logistic regression. Mendelian randomization (MR) was employed to identify potential OPC-related drug target genes. RESULTS: We identified 43 OPC risk genetic variants with p < 1E-06, which mapped to 7 independent loci. item.title: Does nasal surgery alter vocal resonance? the acoustic impact of rhinoplasty, septoplasty, and turbinoplasty - a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Karagoz T, Bennett W
item.description:
Authors: Karagoz T, Bennett W
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10609-x
Published: 2026-Oct-04
PMID: 42830355



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nasal surgeries including rhinoplasty, septoplasty, and turbinoplasty are among the most commonly performed otolaryngologic procedures worldwide, with millions of operations conducted annually. The nasal cavity functions as a critical resonator in the vocal tract, contributing to voice quality through complex acoustic coupling mechanisms. Alterations in nasal anatomy may theoretically modify vocal resonance characteristics, yet the clinical significance and comparative effects across different surgical procedures remain incompletely understood. This systematic review aimed to synthesize current evidence on acoustic voice changes following rhinoplasty, septoplasty, and turbinoplasty, comparing the magnitude and clinical relevance of alterations across procedure types. METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we conducted a comprehensive systematic search across six databases (PubMed MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Google Scholar) through December 2023. Eligible studies included prospective or retrospective investigations measuring objective acoustic parameters (nasalance, formant frequencies, fundamental frequency, voice quality indices) or subjective voice outcomes before and after nasal surgery in adult patients. Studies were stratified by surgical procedure type. Quality assessment employed modified Newcastle-Ottawa Scale criteria for observational studies. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed for septoplasty nasalance outcomes where sufficient data homogeneity existed. GRADE framework was applied to assess certainty of evidence. RESULTS: From 832 initial records, 676 unique studies underwent title/abstract screening, with 189 full-text articles assessed for eligibility. Forty-three studies met inclusion criteria (septoplasty: n=26, rhinoplasty: n=11, turbinoplasty: n=5, combined procedures: n=1), encompassing 2,039 patients. Meta-analysis of 12 septoplasty studies (N=600 patients) demonstrated a pooled mean increase in nasalance scores for nasal phonemes of 17.2 percentage points (95% CI: 15.0-19.4, p<0.001) with substantial heterogeneity (I²=66.1%). Subgroup analysis showed consistent effects across prospective (n=11 studies, 18.6 pp, 95% CI: 14.8-22.4) and retrospective (n=1 study, 11.2 pp, 95% CI: 8.4-14.0) study designs. Rhinoplasty investigations (n=399 patients) showed variable effects on formant frequencies F3-F5, with professional voice users exhibiting greater sensitivity to acoustic changes. Turbinoplasty studies (n=224 patients) revealed intermediate effects. Quality assessment identified 27 high-quality studies (63%), 16 moderate-quality (37%), and 0 low-quality (0%). GRADE assessment indicated very low certainty for septoplasty nasalance outcomes and low certainty for rhinoplasty and turbinoplasty outcomes. Funnel plot analysis and Egger's regression test (t=1.34, df=10, p=0.21) indicated no statistically significant funnel plot asymmetry. Trim-and-fill analysis imputed zero studies, leaving the pooled estimate unchanged; these analyses should be interpreted cautiously given the small number of studies and substantial heterogeneity. CONCLUSIONS: .Available observational evidence suggests that nasal surgery may be associated with measurable alterations in vocal resonance. Septoplasty was associated with increased nasalance (pooled increase 17.2 percentage points, 95% CI: 15.0-19.4), while rhinoplasty studies reported variable changes in higher formant frequencies and turbinoplasty studies reported intermediate acoustic effects. The clinical significance of these changes remains uncertain, and limited observational evidence suggests that professional voice users may be more sensitive to subtle acoustic alterations. Preoperative counseling should address potential voice changes, particularly for individuals with high vocal demands. Future research should employ standardized acoustic protocols and longer follow-up periods to better characterize recovery trajectories and identify patient subgroups at risk for clinically significant voice alterations.

Abstract:

item.title: YRNA1 expression as a candidate prognostic biomarker in oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma: an exploratory cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Fazel F, Koopaie M, Manifar S, Razavi AE, Karamad N

Authors: Fazel F, Koopaie M, Manifar S, Razavi AE, Karamad N

Published: 2026-Oct-03

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma (OTSCC) is an aggressive cancer with a 5-year survival of about 60%, highlighting the need for improved molecular risk stratification. Y RNAs (YRNAs) are small non-coding RNAs implicated in tumor progression, but their prognostic role in OTSCC is unclear. This exploratory retrospective cohort study assessed the prognostic value of YRNA1 expression in 26 patients with primary OTSCC who underwent surgical treatment between 2021 and 2022. DESIGN: YRNA1 expression in tumor tissue was quantified using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), and associations with clinicopathological features and 3-year disease-specific survival were analyzed using nonparametric tests, Kaplan-Meier analysis, and Cox regression. RESULTS: YRNA1 expression was significantly higher in patients who died within 3 years of surgery than in those surviving beyond 3 years (p = 0.020) and showed a moderate positive correlation with T stage and death during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly poorer survival in patients with high YRNA1 expression compared with those with low expression (log-rank p = 0.020). In an exploratory multivariable Cox model, restricted to T stage and YRNA1 expression to avoid overfitting given the limited number of events (11 deaths), YRNA1 expression showed prognostic potential. Each one-unit increase in log₂-transformed YRNA1 expression was associated with a 43% increase in the hazard of OTSCC-related death (HR = 1.43, 95% CI: 1.12-2.03; p = 0.049). However, these findings are exploratory and require validation in larger cohorts. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated YRNA1 expression is associated with poorer disease-specific survival in this cohort of patients with OTSCC, suggesting potential prognostic relevance that requires validation in larger, independent cohorts.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Induction chemotherapy proves critical in hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (HPSCC). However, the mechanisms of acquired resistance to induction chemotherapy have not been fully elucidated yet. METHODS: Nine patients with HPSCC who showed an initial response to IC followed by progression and had available paired paraffin-embedded tissue samples were retrospectively analysed. Whole exome sequencing and functional validation were performed in both in vivo and in vitro experiments using CRISPR-Cas9-mediated knockout and mutant variant transfection. Among the newly emerged variants, alterations in ENPP1, ALK, and ATP10B were notable for potential functional relevance. CONCLUSION: Our study identifies ENPP1 mutation as one of the key genetic drivers of recurrence, mediating both chemotherapy resistance and immunomodulation.

item.title: Concurrent Versus Sequential PD-1 Blockade With Locoregional Radiotherapy After Chemoimmunotherapy in De Novo Metastatic Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Landmark Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Wu L, He J, Zhou Z, Luo R, Li C, Tang L, Mai H, Liu L
item.description:
Authors: Wu L, He J, Zhou Z, Luo R, Li C, Tang L, Mai H, Liu L
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108164
Published: 2026-Oct-03
PMID: 42828792



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chemoimmunotherapy followed by consolidative locoregional radiotherapy has increasingly been used for selected patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (dmNPC). However, whether PD-1 blockade should be continued concurrently during locoregional radiotherapy (LRRT) remains uncertain. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 238 patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma who received platinum-based chemotherapy plus anti-PD-1 therapy followed by definitive locoregional radiotherapy. A 12-month landmark analysis was performed to reduce immortal time bias, and inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to balance baseline and treatment-related characteristics. Recursive partitioning analysis incorporating disease burden, pretreatment lactate dehydrogenase, post-chemoimmunotherapy Epstein-Barr virus DNA clearance, and radiological response was used for risk stratification. Longitudinal absolute lymphocyte counts were evaluated after radiotherapy. RESULTS: Among 238 patients, 185 received concurrent PD-1 blockade during locoregional radiotherapy and 53 did not. After weighting and landmark adjustment, concurrent PD-1 blockade was associated with inferior progression-free survival (PFS) (weighted hazard ratio, 3.189; 95% CI, 1.352-7.524; P=0.008). Distant metastasis-free survival was also inferior in the concurrent group, whereas locoregional recurrence-free survival was similar between groups. Among the four observed treatment patterns, the sandwich strategy, defined as chemoimmunotherapy followed by LRRT without concurrent PD-1 blockade and with subsequent maintenance immunotherapy, showed the most favorable outcomes. In the landmark-adjusted comparison restricted to the full-course and sandwich strategies, the sandwich strategy remained associated with superior PFS (hazard ratio, 0.254; 95% CI, 0.078-0.821; P=0.022). Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested a less favorable outcome pattern with concurrent PD-1 blockade among high-risk patients, although individual subgroup sizes were limited. Persistent lymphopenia at 3 months after radiotherapy was associated with poor outcomes, particularly among patients receiving concurrent PD-1 blockade. CONCLUSION: In conclusion, among patients with dmNPC treated with first-line chemoimmunotherapy followed by definitive LRRT, concurrent PD-1 blockade during LRRT was not associated with improved survival outcomes and was linked to inferior PFS and DMFS in an IPTW-adjusted landmark analysis. Exploratory analyses suggested potential heterogeneity according to baseline risk and post-radiotherapy immune recovery, but these findings were limited by small subgroup sizes. Prospective studies are warranted to define the optimal sequencing of PD-1 blockade and LRRT.

item.title: Safety and feasibility of drainless day-case parotidectomy: an 8-year retrospective cohort study from a tertiary centre.

item.description:
Authors: So CP, Chan C, Campbell A, Manickavasagam J
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10595-0

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Our retrospective study in 2025 found that the use of haemostatic agents in drainless outpatient parotidectomy (DLOP) is associated with an increased risk of seroma/sialoma formation and possible increase in infection risk. The aim of this study was to compare additional complication rates between DLOP and drained inpatient parotidectomy (DIP) in our centre. The secondary aim was to compare postoperative length of hospital stay between the two groups. Patient, surgical and lesion characteristics were compared between DLOP and DIP. Postoperative complications (facial nerve palsy, post-operative haematoma, Frey's syndrome, ear numbness and flap tip necrosis) and postoperative length of stay of DLOP and DIP were evaluated. Logistic regression analysis was used to determine the factors associated with postoperative complication and failure of same day discharge. RESULTS: 72.6% (n = 82) and 27.4% (n = 31) of patients underwent DLOP and DIP respectively. Haemostatic agents were used in a significantly higher percentage of patients who underwent DLOP (59.8%) vs. DIP (12.9%) (p < 0.01). In DLOP group, a significantly higher percentage of small lesions (≤ 35 mm) were observed (p = 0.03). Complication rates were not significantly different between both groups. item.title: Whole-blood versus laboratory intraoperative parathyroid hormone assays and optimisation of intraoperative monitoring during parathyroidectomy: A retrospective cohort study.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Intraoperative parathyroid hormone (IOPTH) monitoring supports focused parathyroidectomy by confirming biochemical response after gland excision, but standard assays may be logistically burdensome. We compared a whole-blood POC IOPTH assay (NBCL CONNECT) with a standard laboratory assay and evaluated candidate IOPTH criteria and sampling timepoints. METHODS: We performed a single-centre retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing parathyroidectomy for primary hyperparathyroidism with IOPTH monitoring over an 18-month period. Paired samples were collected pre-incision, pre-excision, and approximately 5 and 10 min post-excision and analysed using NBCL CONNECT assay performed in theatre, and the laboratory PTH assay performed in the hospital laboratory. The reference outcome was early biochemical success defined by postoperative calcium normalisation and appropriate postoperative PTH profile during the postoperative period. Diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV) was assessed for prespecified IOPTH criteria at 5 and 10 min. RESULTS: Among 103 patients, early biochemical success was achieved in 98 (95.1%). Across evaluated criteria, the laboratory assay demonstrated higher overall diagnostic performance than NBCL CONNECT at both 5 and 10 min (Online Resource 1). For NBCL CONNECT, the prespecified 10-minute criterion (> 50% PTH decline from the lower pre-excision value) yielded a PPV of 96.9% (95% CI 89.3-99.6) and NPV of 51.4% (95% CI 34.0-68.6). CONCLUSION: Whole-blood POC IOPTH using NBCL CONNECT provides a practical intraoperative adjunct but has limited negative predictive value. A 10-minute sample interpreted as a > 50% decline from the lower pre-excision value maximised diagnostic performance within this cohort, supporting a rule-in role for confirming adequacy of excision while cautioning against reliance on a negative POC result alone.

METHODS: We analyzed 88 consecutive H&N MCC patients (2000-2022) by age (< 75 vs. ≥ 75 years). OS was estimated by Kaplan-Meier analysis and MCC-specific death with competing-risks methods (cause-specific Cox regression). RESULTS: Of 88 patients, 57% were ≥ 75 years; older patients underwent less surgery but received RT at similar rates. Age ≥ 75 dominated OS (5-year 23% vs. 71%; adjusted HR 3.24). The 5-year cumulative incidence of MCC-specific death was higher in older patients (42% vs. 23%) but was not independent after adjustment (cause-specific HR 2.02, p = 0.10); competing non-MCC mortality was far higher (31% vs. 6%). Six of 11 ICI-treated patients (55%) were alive at 1.9 years. CONCLUSIONS: Elderly patients undergo less surgery yet receive equivalent RT. Age dominates overall survival, but this mainly reflects competing non-MCC mortality rather than a cancer-specific effect; age-tailored, competing-risk-aware protocols are needed.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment-related symptoms and toxicities are common in Head and Neck Cancer (HNC) patients undergoing chemoradiation (CRT). This underscores the importance of timely interventions and effective symptom and toxicity monitoring strategies to mitigate complications and improve quality of life (QoL). Traditional clinician and care team assessments often underreport patient symptoms, leading to urgent care and emergency room admissions, referred to as health care utilization (HCU). In contrast, electronically captured patient-reported outcomes (ePROs) are associated with improved survival, better health-related QoL, and lower HCU. Wearable activity monitors (WAMs) offer an additional method for continuous monitoring, enabling clinicians to detect symptoms and toxicities more efficiently and respond rapidly to patient needs. METHODS: 12 HNC patients were assessed with ePROs and WAMs during CRT. RESULTS: HNC patients undergoing CRT are receptive to ePRO and WAM-based monitoring. item.title: Normal Pregnancy and Voice: A PRISMA-ScR Scoping Review of Laryngeal and Vocal Outcomes.
item.dc:creator: Boyd JM, Williams JT, McGowan R, Kervin S, Kwak PE, Morse E
item.description:
Authors: Boyd JM, Williams JT, McGowan R, Kervin S, Kwak PE, Morse E
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.70953
Published: 2026-Oct-02
PMID: 42825795



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pregnancy produces physiologic adaptations that may affect laryngeal tissues, respiratory support for phonation, and voice quality. We performed a scoping review exploring the influence of pregnancy on voice and laryngeal outcomes. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, CINAHL, and Web of Science. REVIEW METHODS: A scoping review was conducted per PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches of PubMed, CINAHL, and Web of Science yielded 1350 studies screened in Covidence by two reviewers. Of 107 full texts reviewed, 22 met inclusion criteria. We included human studies in which pregnancy was the primary exposure and voice-related outcomes were measured. Pregnancy-specific animal studies were included when modeling mechanisms of laryngeal change. RESULTS: Twenty-two studies met inclusion criteria and were grouped into domains: acoustic/aerodynamic (n = 16), patient-reported/perceptual (n = 12), physiologic laryngeal (n = 5), mechanistic animal studies (n = 4), singing voice (n = 4), and respiratory (n = 1); several studies contributed to multiple domains. Acoustic measures (fundamental frequency, jitter, shimmer) were generally unchanged, while multiple studies reported reduced maximum phonation time (MPT) during pregnancy. Subjective voice measures tended to worsen, and singer studies reported reduced vocal range and timbre changes. Physiologic studies noted increased vocal fold edema and reduced motility, most prominent in the third trimester. Mechanistic models supported hormone-associated mucosal changes and altered laryngeal protein expression. CONCLUSIONS: The literature on voice changes during pregnancy is limited and heterogeneous, with evidence concentrated in late pregnancy. Pregnancy is more consistently associated with reduced phonatory efficiency and worse perceived voice function than with major acoustic vocal changes. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: N/A.

item.title: Biological Biomarkers in Proliferative Verrucous Leukoplakia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Alkeheli MF, Othman HI
item.description:
Authors: Alkeheli MF, Othman HI
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70520
Published: 2026-Oct-02

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To synthesise biological biomarker evidence in proliferative verrucous leukoplakia/proliferative leukoplakia and quantify malignant transformation using eligible longitudinal evidence. METHODS: Primary human biomarker studies and longitudinal studies reporting extractable malignant-transformation events and denominators were systematically reviewed. Biomarker evidence was synthesised narratively. Malignant-transformation proportions were pooled using a random-effects model, with conservative handling of potentially overlapping cohorts. RESULTS: Forty-one publications contributed to the biomarker synthesis, spanning genetic, genomic, DNA-ploidy, epigenetic, transcriptomic, proteomic, immunohistochemical, immunologic, viral, microbiome, salivary, and circulating markers. No biomarker had sufficient independent validation for clinical diagnostic or prognostic use. Twenty independent or conservatively non-overlapping study estimates comprising 745 patients and 243 malignant-transformation events contributed to the meta-analysis. The pooled malignant-transformation proportion was 34.13% (95% confidence interval 26.62-42.53), with substantial heterogeneity and a 95% prediction interval of 13.85%-62.56%. Results remained stable in sensitivity and leave-one-out analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Diverse biological alterations have been reported, but none currently supports routine biomarker-based diagnosis or individual risk stratification. Malignant transformation is frequent, although substantial between-study variability limits interpretation of the pooled estimate as an individual patient risk.

item.title: Determining the Causal Effect of Neurotrophic Tropomyosin Receptor Kinase Gene Fusions on Survival Prognosis for Adult Patients With Advanced Cancers.

Authors: Krebs E, Tamvada N, Weymann D, Lim HJ, Chia S, Ho C, Regier DA
Journal: JCO precision oncology | DOI: 10.1200/PO-26-00281
Published: 2026-Oct-01

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Uncertainty about the prognostic significance of neurotrophic tropomyosin receptor kinase (NTRK) fusions complicates clinical decisions and interpretation of survival outcomes in oncology care. Drawing on the largest cohort of NTRK fusion-positive (NTRK+) patients, we establish the prognostic effect of NTRK fusions in adults with advanced cancers. METHODS: We used a large real-world clinicogenomic research database from the United States to emulate a pragmatic randomized trial that determines the causal effect of harboring an NTRK gene fusion (NTRK+) on survival prognosis for adult patients with advanced solid tumors. We 1:1 matched NTRK+ patients to patients with no identified NTRK genomic alterations (NTRK-) using a machine learning matching approach. Excluding patients who received TRK inhibitors, we conducted stratified matching within common tumor groups. We used Kaplan-Meier and Weibull regression survival analyses and estimated the difference in restricted mean survival time (RMST) over 1-, 2-, 3-, and 5-year study periods. RESULTS: We included 68,145 NTRK- patients for matching to 73 NTRK+ patients within seven tumor groups, including colorectal (n = 22), non-small cell lung (n = 13), sarcoma (n = 13), breast (n = 10), head and neck (n = 7), neuroendocrine (n = 4), and prostate (n = 4), and 14 NTRK+ patients representing eight other cancers. The difference in overall survival over 1 year was statistically significant using the Kaplan-Meier estimate (P = .008), Weibull regression (hazard ratio, 2.105 [95% CI, 1.207 to 3.673]), and RMST (-50 days [95% CI, -96 to -5]; P = .029). Differences were also statistically different at 2 years and 3 years. At 5 years, no survival differences were statistically significant. CONCLUSION: In this large real-world target trial emulation, NTRK gene fusions were associated with clinically meaningful reductions in overall survival among adults with advanced cancers not treated with TRK inhibitors. These findings clarify the prognostic role of NTRK fusions and inform clinical interpretation of outcomes in routine oncology.

item.title: Anticoagulation Outcomes in Nursing Home Residents With Atrial Fibrillation and ADL Disability.
item.dc:creator: Chen Q, Singer D, Yang CT, Pritchard KT, Kim DH, Lin KJ
item.description:
Authors: Chen Q, Singer D, Yang CT, Pritchard KT, Kim DH, Lin KJ
Journal: JAMA network open | DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.37533
Published: 2026-Oct-01
PMID: 42832198



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Long-term nursing home residents with atrial fibrillation (AF) and activities of daily living (ADL) disability are at high risk of bleeding and death, making the net benefit of anticoagulation uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To compare the association of oral anticoagulant (OAC) use vs nonuse with ischemic stroke and major bleeding in long-term nursing home residents with AF and ADL disability. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used US Medicare claims linked with the Minimum Data Set (January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2022). Nursing home residents with nonvalvular AF and impairment in 3 or more ADLs were included. Three cohorts comparing use of apixaban, rivaroxaban, or warfarin with nonuse were constructed using incidence-density sampling. EXPOSURES: Initiation of apixaban, rivaroxaban, or warfarin use. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were ischemic stroke, major bleeding, and their composite. Propensity score (PS) matching balanced 111 covariates. Adjusted rate ratios (ARRs) with 95% CIs were estimated. Tipping-point analyses assessed the relative weighting ischemic stroke vs major bleeding required to favor anticoagulation. Direct active-comparator analyses compared apixaban with rivaroxaban and warfarin. RESULTS: The study comprised 26 940 nursing home residents (median [IQR] age, 82 [74,88] years; 17 504 [65.0%] female), including PS-matched cohorts of 7600 residents receiving apixaban, 2654 receiving rivaroxaban, and 3216 receiving warfarin. Compared with nonuse, use of all OACs was associated with lower rates of ischemic stroke (apixaban: ARR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.38-0.73; rivaroxaban: ARR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.27-0.87; warfarin: ARR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.25-0.88) and higher rates of major bleeding (apixaban: ARR, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.29-2.03; rivaroxaban: ARR, 2.68; 95% CI, 1.84-3.93; warfarin: ARR, 3.02; 95% CI, 2.15-4.25). Only apixaban was not associated with a higher composite outcome (ARR, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.90-1.30), whereas rivaroxaban (ARR, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.20-2.18) and warfarin (ARR, 1.99; 95% CI, 1.50-2.63) were associated with higher rates. Findings were consistent across frailty strata, although stroke reduction with apixaban was attenuated among frail individuals. Tipping-point analyses indicated a more favorable benefit-risk balance for apixaban than for rivaroxaban or warfarin. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among nursing home residents with AF and ADL disability, OAC use was associated with lower ischemic stroke but higher major bleeding rates than nonuse. Apixaban demonstrated the most favorable benefit-risk profile among the OACs evaluated. These findings may inform individualized anticoagulation decisions.

item.title: Markers of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 regression and subsequent risk of CIN3.

Published: 2026-Oct-01

Abstract:
Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) grade 2 (CIN2), a precursor to cervical cancer, can regress without treatment, but the prognostic value of different regression markers remains unclear. Using electronic medical records from 5,938 women with newly detected CIN2 managed with delayed treatment at Kaiser Permanente Northern California, we estimated the frequency of histologic, cytologic, and virologic regression within 1 year of CIN2 diagnosis and the subsequent 3-year risk of CIN grade 3 or worse (CIN3+). Histologic regression was common but remained associated with appreciable subsequent CIN3+ risk. In contrast, HPV-negative results were associated with lower subsequent CIN3+ risk than normal histology or normal cytology (2.8% vs. 7.0% and 4.2%, respectively; both p < 0.001). Combined HPV-negative and normal cytology results identified the lowest risk group (1.3%; all pairwise comparisons, p < 0.001). These findings suggest that HPV clearance may be a more informative endpoint for therapeutic trials and marker for guiding surveillance of CIN2.

item.title: Type II RAF Inhibitor Tovorafenib in Recurrent/Refractory Melanoma or Other Solid Tumors With BRAF Fusions or CRAF/RAF1 Fusions or Amplification: Phase II FIRELIGHT-1 Substudy.
item.dc:creator: Vieito M, Cabanas EG, Mehmi I, Gaudy-Marqueste C, O'Neil BH, Medina TM, Body AL, Arance A, Kummar S, Najjar YG, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Vieito M, Cabanas EG, Mehmi I, Gaudy-Marqueste C, O'Neil BH, Medina TM, Body AL, Arance A, Kummar S, Najjar YG, et al.
Journal: JCO precision oncology | DOI: 10.1200/PO-25-01187
Published: 2026-Oct-01

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Tovorafenib is an oral, selective, CNS-penetrant, type II inhibitor of BRAF and CRAF. BRAF fusions and CRAF/RAF1 fusions and amplifications are rare oncogenic drivers in many solid tumors. The phase II DAY101-102a substudy of FIRELIGHT-1 (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04985604) investigated the efficacy and safety of tovorafenib monotherapy in recurrent/refractory solid tumors with structural alterations in BRAF or CRAF. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients ≥12 years of age with a recurrent/refractory solid tumor with a BRAF fusion or CRAF fusion or amplification were enrolled into a melanoma cohort or tumor-agnostic cohort. The primary end point was overall response rate (ORR), as assessed by investigators. Tovorafenib was administered at 600 mg once weekly (adult dose), continuously, in 28-day cycles. RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were enrolled; eight in the melanoma cohort and 15 in the tumor-agnostic cohort. The median age was 53 years (range, 21-71), and 57% of patients had ≥2 lines of prior therapy. Fourteen patients had tumors with BRAF fusion, six CRAF fusion, two CRAF amplification, and one CRAF fusions and amplification. The median duration of tovorafenib treatment was 5.3 months (range, 0.8-22.5). The ORR was 43% (10/23 patients), including 50% (4/8) in patients with melanoma and 40% (6/15) in patients with other tumors. The median time to response was 1.8 months. The median duration of response was 9.2 months. The most common treatment-related adverse events (any grade) were anemia (39%), pruritus (30%), increased creatine phosphokinase (26%), and rash (26%). CONCLUSION: Tovorafenib demonstrated single-agent clinical activity in solid tumors with BRAF fusions or CRAF fusions or amplification and had a manageable safety profile. Tovorafenib may offer a new targeted treatment option for adult patients with tumors harboring these rare genomic driver alterations.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Despite increasing use of core needle biopsy (CNB) for salivary gland lesions, its clinical utility requires further evaluation. As previous studies have focused mainly on surgically confirmed lesions, this study evaluated the diagnostic utility and reliability of CNB for major salivary gland lesions irrespective of treatment modality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 217 patients who underwent major salivary gland CNB at the Helsinki University Hospital (HUS, Helsinki, Finland) between 2020 and 2022. Patients were classified into surgical and follow-up groups, with follow-up data review of patient records for non-operated patients through the end of 2024. RESULTS: Altogether, 247 CNB samples were obtained from 221 major salivary gland lesions. Ninety-three patients (42%) underwent surgery, and 128 tumors in 124 patients (58%) were followed up only. Based on histologically verified cases, CNB demonstrated 93.8% sensitivity and 98.5% specificity for malignancy, with one false benign and one false malignant result. No malignancies were identified in the follow-up group during a minimum of 2-year follow-up. CONCLUSION: CNB is a highly accurate diagnostic tool for salivary gland tumors and may facilitate the identification of lesions that can be safely managed without surgery.

item.title: Protocol for the REVELIO test-track pilot study: A randomised, controlled, single-centre trial in healthy recreational cannabis users investigating real-time in-vehicle detection of cannabis-impaired driving.
item.dc:creator: Deuber R, Bechny M, Heck C, Brügger J, Pfäffli M, Jovanova M, Fleisch E, Wortmann F, Weinmann W
item.description:
Authors: Deuber R, Bechny M, Heck C, Brügger J, Pfäffli M, Jovanova M, Fleisch E, Wortmann F, Weinmann W
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0349328
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42821661



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Driving under the influence of cannabis is associated with impaired cognitive and psychomotor performance and an increased risk of traffic accidents. Reliable real-time in-vehicle systems for detecting cannabis-related driving impairment are currently lacking; but hold great potential for improving road safety. METHODS: This protocol describes the REVELIO test-track pilot study: a randomised, controlled, open-label, interventional, single-centre trial. The study assesses the feasibility and methodological requirements for developing and evaluating a multimodal in-vehicle detection approach using vehicle and driver state data. A total of 45 healthy recreational cannabis users will be enrolled and randomly allocated to an intervention or a reference control group. During the main study day, all participants will undergo biological sampling for tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and related metabolites, as well as pre-driving assessments, followed by a sober baseline driving session on a closed test track using a dual-pedal vehicle with a certified driving instructor onboard. Participants in the intervention group will then receive a single controlled inhalative cannabis dose (target 0.67 mg THC per kg body weight), while the reference group will receive no cannabis. All participants will subsequently complete three additional standardized 50-minute driving sessions at predefined time points up to approximately six hours after administration, following identical schedules to enable within- and between-group comparisons. Between driving sessions, structured breaks will include recovery periods, repeated biological sampling, and traffic-medical, traffic-psychological, and pre-driving performance assessments, to characterise the temporal dynamics of cannabis-related impairment. DISCUSSION: Multimodal data will be collected, including vehicle controller area network (CAN) data, driver monitoring camera (DMC) data, physiological signals using wearables, and biological samples (capillary blood, breath, oral fluid. Machine-learning-based models will be developed and evaluated to distinguish sober from cannabis-influenced driving states under controlled conditions. Secondary analyses will examine changes in driving performance over time and associations between functional measures and biological THC concentrations. As an exploratory pilot study conducted on a secured test track, the protocol aims to generate standardized reference data and quantitative performance metrics to inform both feasibility and system design considerations. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07401628).

item.title: Ticagrelor and gut microbiota: Absence of pharmacokinetic interaction in vitro and in vivo studies.
item.dc:creator: Qu P, Gao Y, Li X, Yang L, Tang J, Chen M, Wang Y, Peng Y, Jiang J, Huang W, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Qu P, Gao Y, Li X, Yang L, Tang J, Chen M, Wang Y, Peng Y, Jiang J, Huang W, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0359660
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42821516



Abstract:
Ticagrelor, a commonly used antiplatelet medication, has been found to exhibit considerable inter-individual pharmacodynamic variability. Recent studies have revealed a close relationship between pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, both of which can be influenced by gut microbiota. In this study, we explored whether the pharmacokinetics of ticagrelor is mediated by intestinal flora. We enrolled 22 healthy participants to assess the clinical pharmacokinetic profiles of ticagrelor and its metabolite AR-C124910XX after a single oral dose of ticagrelor. The fecal microbial compositions of individuals who exhibited distinct pharmacokinetic parameters were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Additionally, we conducted experiments involving the co-incubation of ticagrelor with fecal bacteria and a systematic exploration of the pharmacokinetics of ticagrelor in pseudo-germ-free (PGF) rats to illustrate the role of gut microbiota in ticagrelor metabolism, both in vitro and in vivo. Our findings revealed a three-fold difference in the bioavailability of ticagrelor among individuals. However, no difference was found in the composition of gut microbiota among individuals with different pharmacokinetic parameters. Quantitative analysis showed that gut microbiota cannot directly metabolize ticagrelor. Furthermore, there were no significant differences in AUC(0-48), AUC(0-∞), and Cmax between ticagrelor and AR-C124910XX in PGF rats compared to normal control, either by single intragastric or intravenous administration. In conclusion, these findings suggest that gut microbiota has no impact on the pharmacokinetics of ticagrelor.

item.title: Testosterone Inhibition and Risk of Laryngeal and Hypopharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma in Men.
item.dc:creator: Gottlieb-Vedi E, Santoni G, Hammarstedt-Nordenvall L, Xie SH, Lagergren J
item.description:

Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma most commonly occur in men. It has been hypothesized that testosterone explains this sex difference, but there is a lack of research on the topic. 5α-Reductase inhibitors (5-ARIs) are common medications used for men with benign hyperplasia that inhibit the conversion of testosterone to the bioactive form dihydrotestosterone and, thus, have anti-androgenic properties. OBJECTIVE: To examine whether use of 5-ARIs is associated with lower risk of laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma in men. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This population-based cohort study included men in the Swedish Prescribed Drugs and Health Cohort from July 1, 2005, to December 31, 2022, with follow-up until December 31, 2023. EXPOSURE: At least 2 dispensations of 5-ARIs within 2 years during the study period. Users of 5-ARIs were compared with 5 times as many age- and date-matched men without history of 5-ARI use. MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: The main outcome was a new diagnosis of laryngeal or hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma during follow-up. Multivariable Cox regression provided hazard ratios with 95% CIs, adjusted for alcohol overconsumption, tobacco smoking, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes. RESULTS: A total of 253 010 users of 5-ARIs and 1 265 050 nonusers were included (median [IQR] age, 74 [67-80] years). The median (IQR) follow-up time was 5.8 (2.7-10.1) years among the 5-ARI users and 4.7 (1.0-9.4) years among the nonusers. Laryngeal or hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma was diagnosed in 215 (0.1%) of the 5-ARI users and 1131 (0.1%) of the nonusers. Use of 5-ARIs was associated with a 17% lower risk of laryngeal or hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma compared to nonusers (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.72-0.96). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study, use of 5-ARIs was associated with a decreased relative risk of hypopharyngeal and laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma. This supports a possible partial role of testosterone in the origin and male predominance of these tumors.

item.title: Long-Term Opioid Use Following Radiation or Chemoradiation for Head and Neck Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Desai O, Kotler A, Virk J, Agner K, Wells J, Nguyen M, Reed D, Tella K, Alvarez D, Koempel A, et al.
item.description:

Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Patients with head and neck cancer represent a vulnerable patient population for potential chronic opioid use. Prior institutional studies on chronic opioid use had limited sample sizes, and the incidence of and risk factors for chronic opioid use need further investigation. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the proportion of patients with opioid use and factors associated with opioid use 3 months following chemoradiation or radiation treatment for head and neck cancer. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This single-institution cohort study at The Ohio State Comprehensive Cancer Center included patients diagnosed with nonmetastatic head and neck cancer between October 2011 and December 2023 who received definitive radiation or chemoradiation. EXPOSURE: Receipt of definitive radiation or chemoradiation. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was opioid use 3 months after completing radiation in the entire cohort. Logistic multivariable analysis was performed to evaluate variables associated with opioid use at this time point. Secondary end points were opioid use at 6 months and time to first opioid use in an opioid-naive patient subgroup. RESULTS: A total of 789 patients met the study's inclusion criteria (639 men [81.0%]; median age, 61 years [IQR, 55-68 years]). Median follow-up was 46.7 months (IQR, 31.1-56.1 months). Between diagnosis and 6 months following radiation, 750 patients (95.1%) received prescription opioids. At 3 and 6 months following radiation, 552 (70.0%) and 373 (47.3%) patients, respectively, continued taking prescription opioids. Patients were more likely to be taking opioids at 3 months following radiation if they were former smokers (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 1.55; 95% CI, 1.04-2.31), were referred to palliative care (AOR, 3.90; 95% CI, 2.57-6.09), or had taken opioids prior to radiation (AOR, 2.57; 95% CI, 1.82-3.63). Among 296 patients who were opioid-naive prior to radiation (37.5%), time to first opioid use was shorter for those with underweight status (adjusted hazard ratio [AHR], 7.36; 95% CI, 3.40-15.90) and those referred to palliative care (AHR, 1.42; 95% CI, 1.10-1.83). Of the opioid-naive patients, 171 (57.8%) and 112 (37.8%) continued taking opioids at 3 and 6 months following radiation, respectively. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study, 70.0% and 47.3% of patients with head and neck cancer continued taking opioids at 3 and 6 months following treatment, respectively. Factors associated with opioid use at 3 months included prior opioid use, former smoking status, and palliative care referral. These findings suggest that targeted opioid stewardship programs that consider both analgesia and long-term dependency risk are merited.

item.dc:creator: Xing J, Han X, Hu X, Meng L, Qu L, Nipp RD, Yabroff KR, Jiang C
item.description:

Journal: JAMA network open | DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.37508
Published: 2026-Oct-01
PMID: 42821259



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Medical debt affects millions of US residents and has been associated with higher cancer mortality. Whether medical debt burden is associated with incidence of advanced stage cancer, a key determinant of survival, remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between medical debt and cancer incidence in the US. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cross-sectional study used ecological county-level data linking 2016 medical debt with age-adjusted incidence rates of 9 cancers from January 1, 2017, to December 31, 2021. The study included 2958 US counties with available data on medical debt in collections and cancer incidence rates. Population-based data were obtained and analyzed from January 11, 2025, to February 15, 2026. EXPOSURE: Percentage of residents with any medical debt in collections in 2016. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Age-adjusted all-stage and late-stage (regional or distant) cancer incidence rates per 100 000 person-years from 2017 to 2021. Multivariable models adjusted for urban-rural status, Social Vulnerability Index (SVI), primary care physician density, and states were used to estimate differences in age-adjusted incidence rates of cancer associated with county-level medical debt burden. RESULTS: Among the 2958 US counties included in the analysis, 1154 (39.0%) were urban and 1804 (61.0%) were rural. The mean (SD) prevalence of medical debt in collections was 21.1% (9.6%), with a mean (SD) primary care physician density of 0.54 (0.35) physicians per 1000 population. The prevalence of medical debt ranged from 1.2% to 51.8%. The mean (SD) medical debt prevalence was higher in rural than urban counties (21.5% [10.0%] vs 20.5% [8.9%]; P = .007) and in counties in the highest vs lowest SVI quartile (27.4% [9.0%] vs 13.9% [6.9%]; P < .001). After adjustment, each 10percentage point increase in county-level medical debt was associated with a higher incidence of late-stage lung cancer (5.15 [95% CI, 4.62-5.68] additional cases per 100 000 person-years), colorectal cancer (0.69 [95% CI, 0.44-0.94] additional cases per 100 000 person-years), cervical cancer (0.39 [95% CI, 0.23-0.55] additional cases per 100 000 person-years), melanoma (0.59 [95% CI, 0.48-0.70] additional cases per 100 000 person-years), kidney and renal pelvis cancer (0.38 [95% CI, 0.27-0.49] additional cases per 100 000 person-years), bladder cancer (0.24 [95% CI, 0.16-0.32] additional cases per 100 000 person-years), and head and neck cancer (0.92 [95% CI, 0.77-1.07] additional cases per 100 000 person-years). Similar patterns were observed for overall cancer incidence. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cross-sectional study of US counties, higher medical debt burden was associated with higher incidence rates of late-stage and overall cancer across multiple cancer types. These findings suggest that medical debt may reflect structural and financial barriers associated with cancer diagnosis and outcomes at the population level.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: National Standards for Cancer Survivorship Care (i.e., survivorship standards) were developed as policy, process, and assessment standards to guide quality of survivorship care across all cancer settings. This descriptive study uses two methods to provide a picture of the alignment of care for patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) with survivorship standards in an academic health care system in Southeast Texas. METHODS: One method consisted of an anonymous survey of 15 HNC providers' perceptions of alignment of survivorship standards with HNC. A modified kappa score for each standard was computed as proportion of participants' agreement that the standard was relevant to the institutions' HNC care. Scores ranged from 1 (highly relevant) to 0 (not relevant). The second method analyzed encounters over a 1-year period after diagnosis using electronic health record (EHR) data of 438 patients with HNC from the same institution. Statistical analysis included descriptive statistics and generalized linear models. RESULTS: Modified kappa scores showed the institution's processes to provide HNC survivorship services were more aligned with survivorship standards (process = 0.60) than institutional policies or assessments (policies = 0.28; assessments = 0.29). CONCLUSION: The study's cross-cutting themes include need for policies and assessments that increase EHR documentation of HNC survivorship care. IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: The survivorship standards may be useful in developing clinical and informatics infrastructure needed to advance the quality of HNC survivorship care.

item.title: Epstein-Barr virus-attributable cancers among children and adolescents in Europe and North America: a meta-analysis.

item.description:
Authors: Volesky-Avellaneda KD, Tsyruk-Romano O, Hildesheim A, Walter SD, El-Zein M, Friedenreich CM, Brenner DR, Franco EL
Journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute | DOI: 10.1093/jnci/djag344
Published: 2026-Oct-01
PMID: 42820761



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), a common childhood infection, is associated with Burkitt lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, and nasopharyngeal cancer. We estimated the proportion and number of cancers attributable to EBV among individuals aged ≤19 years in Europe and North America in 2022. METHODS: Embase and MEDLINE were searched from inception to August 25th, 2025. Cancer incidence was derived from GLOBOCAN. We included studies where cancer tissue from ≥8 individuals aged ≤19 years residing in Europe or North America were tested for EBV. Pooled EBV prevalence and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using random-effects models. To obtain EBV-attributable cases, pooled prevalence was multiplied by cancer incidence. RESULTS: After screening 17,388 titles/abstracts and 1,084 full-texts, 53 studies met the inclusion criteria for Burkitt lymphoma (9 studies, 433 cases), Hodgkin lymphoma (40 studies, 3197 cases), and nasopharyngeal cancer (4 studies, 62 cases). The pooled prevalence of EBV was 19.7% (CI: 10.2-34.7%, I2=69.5%) in Burkitt lymphoma, 33.4% (CI: 27.4-40.0%, I2=75.6%) in Hodgkin lymphoma, and 96.8% (CI: 88.0-99.2%, I2=0.0) in nasopharyngeal cancer. An estimated 1,166 (2.8%) of 41,366 cancers diagnosed in 2022, were attributable to EBV. These cases comprised 899 Hodgkin lymphomas, 140 Burkitt lymphomas, and 127 nasopharyngeal cancers. The burden was higher among males (3.2% vs 2.3% for females) and those aged 10-14 years (5.0% vs 1.7% for 0-9-year-olds and 3.1% for 15-19-year-olds). CONCLUSION: In 2022, 2.8% of childhood cancers diagnosed in Europe and North America were attributable to EBV.

item.title: Impact of Tranexamic Acid on Head and Neck Free Flap Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Analysis.

item.description:
Authors: Adams G, Fried I, Longfellow GA, Pede C, Monk A, Benaim EH, Tasoulas J, Kimple AJ, Hackman T, Sullivan CB
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.70933
Published: 2026-Oct-01

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is an antifibrinolytic agent studied for its role in reducing perioperative bleeding. While it has shown promise in operations requiring free tissue transfer in plastic surgery, its application in head and neck free flap reconstruction is less documented. This study evaluates the impact of TXA on head and neck free flap surgery outcomes. METHODS: This was a single-institution retrospective cohort study of adult patients who underwent head and neck reconstruction with autologous free tissue transfer between May 2023 and October 2024. Multivariable logistic regression and linear regression were used to evaluate differences between groups. Odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals were used to describe associations. RESULTS: A total of 215 patients were included (15.3% receiving TXA). Patients who received TXA had a higher rate of intraoperative transfusions (p = 0.049). This difference was not observed after adjustment for other factors (p = 0.21). Patients who received TXA had a more stable hemoglobin at Postoperative Day (POD) 1 (-1.84 ± 1.62 vs. -2.77 ± 1.36 g/dL, p = 0.045), however, this difference resolved by POD 7 with no difference in postoperative transfusion rates (p = 0.22). There was no difference in postoperative recipient site, donor site, or medical complications between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Head and neck free flap patients that received TXA had no significant difference in flap outcomes or major thrombotic events. Our results suggest that TXA is a safe option among patients undergoing free tissue transfer for head and neck reconstruction. Further prospective research with larger cohort sizes is needed to elucidate potential benefits.

item.title: Exceptional and Durable Response to Selpercatinib in a Patient with Apparently RET-Negative, HRAS-, and NF1-Mutated Metastatic Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Selpercatinib is approved for RET-mutated medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC); its activity in tumors without detectable RET alterations is uncertain. PATIENT FINDINGS: A 50-year-old woman developed rapidly progressive MTC (Ki-67 = 30%) with extensive liver and bone metastases. Because of severe symptomatic progression, selpercatinib was started urgently, off-label, before molecular testing results were available. She had rapid clinical improvement, marked calcitonin and CEA decline, and a remarkable and durable radiographic partial response until the last follow-up (29 months). SUMMARY: Repeated germline and tumor testing [RET Sanger sequencing, germline whole-exome sequencing, tumor DNA/RNA panel testing, RET Multiplex Ligation-Dependent Probe Amplification (MLPA), tumor whole-genome sequencing] identified no pathogenic or actionable RET variant, indel, copy-number alteration, or fusion. The only somatic alterations found were HRAS p.G13S and truncating NF1 p.R2450*. CONCLUSIONS: This remarkable response to selpercatinib in apparently RET-negative MTC is hypothesis generating and requires confirmation. HRAS/NF1 co-alteration supports RAS/MAPK activation but does not explain sensitivity to selective RET inhibition.

item.title: Pretreatment Cachexia Index Is Associated With Severe Treatment Toxicity and Overall Survival in HPV-Negative Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Savoia G, Hier MP, Sadeghi N, Mlynarek A, Richardson K, Wurzba SDS, Tsien C, Shenouda G, Sultanem K, Bouganim N, et al.

Published: 2026-Oct-01

Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cancer cachexia is characterized by skeletal muscle loss, poor nutrition, and systemic inflammation and is common in head and neck cancer. We evaluated whether the Cachexia Index (CXI) predicts treatment toxicity and survival in HPV-negative HNSCC. METHODS: This study included 353 patients undergoing curative-intent surgery at two McGill University hospitals (2015-2025). Pretreatment CXI was calculated using skeletal muscle index, serum albumin, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. Multivariable logistic and Cox regression assessed associations with severe treatment toxicity (CTCAE grade ≥ 3), overall survival (OS), and disease-free survival. RESULTS: The lowest CXI quintile was independently associated with severe treatment toxicity (OR 2.04, 95% CI 1.07-3.87). The two lowest CXI quintiles were associated with worse OS (HR 3.00 and 2.83), while each 100-unit CXI increase reduced mortality risk by 8.9% (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.86-0.97). CONCLUSIONS: Low pretreatment CXI was independently associated with severe treatment toxicity and poorer overall survival. However, CXI was not independently associated with treatment intolerance or disease-free survival after multivariable adjustment. These findings support further evaluation of CXI as a pretreatment risk stratification tool.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the psychometric performance of the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A) and Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D) in patients with oral lichen planus (OLP) according to clinical phenotype. METHODS: This multicenter SIPMO case-control study included 395 participants: 132 patients with keratotic OLP (K-OLP), 131 with non-keratotic OLP (NK-OLP), and 132 healthy controls (HCs). Internal consistency was assessed with Cronbach's alpha and item discrimination with item-total correlations. HAM-A and HAM-D scores were compared between OLP patients and HCs; phenotype-specific hierarchical regressions identified variables associated with anxiety and depressive symptoms. RESULTS: HAM-A and HAM-D showed satisfactory internal consistency in K-OLP and NK-OLP patients (HAM-A α = 0.877 and 0.858; HAM-D α = 0.768 and 0.766, respectively). Patients with OLP had significantly higher HAM-A and HAM-D scores than age- and sex-matched controls without oral mucosal disease (p = 0.018 and p = 0.002, respectively). Poor sleep quality was independently associated with psychological burden, and pain intensity independently predicted anxiety severity in NK-OLP patients. CONCLUSIONS: HAM-A and HAM-D showed satisfactory psychometric performance in OLP and may support psychological assessment. Somatic and sleep-related symptoms were closely associated with psychological distress.

item.title: Band-Like Chronic Inflammatory Infiltrate in Proliferative Verrucous Leukoplakia: A Meta-Analysis.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Proliferative verrucous leukoplakia is an oral potentially malignant disorder with a difficult diagnosis. A band-like chronic inflammatory infiltrate is frequently described in early lesions, but its prevalence and prognostic relevance remain unclear. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of this feature in proliferative verrucous leukoplakia and assess its prognostic value. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted according to PRISMA guidelines, with protocol registration in PROSPERO (CRD420251249570). Electronic databases and gray literature were searched. Observational studies reporting a band-like chronic inflammatory infiltrate in lesions from patients with proliferative verrucous leukoplakia were included. Data extraction and risk of bias assessment were performed independently. Random effects models estimated pooled prevalence and odds ratios for malignant transformation. RESULTS: Eleven studies including 307 patients were analyzed. The pooled prevalence of a band-like chronic inflammatory infiltrate was 57%. Malignant transformation occurred in 39.5% of cases with this feature and 53% of cases without it. Meta-analysis revealed no statistically significant association between a band-like chronic inflammatory infiltrate and malignant transformation. CONCLUSIONS: Band-like chronic inflammatory infiltrates are common in proliferative verrucous leukoplakia, but current evidence is insufficient to determine whether this feature is associated with malignant transformation and clinically meaningful effects cannot be excluded.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim was to evaluate periodontitis prevalence and severity, and number of RT1 gingival recessions in Oral Lichen Planus (OLP) patients compared with non-OLP controls. METHODS: This case-control study was conducted between 2024 and 2025 at the Oral Medicine Unit, Fondazione Policlinico Universitario A. Gemelli, Rome, Italy. A total of 176 individuals were enrolled: 88 histologically confirmed OLP patients and 88 age/sex-matched controls. Periodontal status was assessed using major clinical indices and classified according to the 2017 AAP/EFP case definition. Ethics Committee UCSC, ID-7603; ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07597616). RESULTS: Periodontitis prevalence was significantly higher in OLP patients than controls (71.6% vs. 51.1%; OR: 2.99; 95% CI: 1.44-6.21, p = 0.03) as was severe periodontitis (48.9% vs. 30.7%; OR: 3.06; 95% CI: 1.44-6.47, p = 0.004). The association with RT1 recessions in the absence of periodontitis suggests a relationship between mucosal inflammation on periodontal tissues and should be further explored.

item.title: Evaluating outcomes of a preoperative nutrition quality improvement program in oral cavity cancer patients: A retrospective analysis.
item.dc:creator: Etemadi AS, Zalaquett NG, Jensen JR, Holger JS, Daher GS, Bogan AW, Davide AD, Price DL, Moore EJ, Tasche KK, et al.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate outcomes of a nursing-led preoperative nutrition screening and referral program in patients undergoing surgery for oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCC). METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted 6 months prior to and 6 months following introduction of a nursing-led Patient-Generated Subjective Global Assessment (PG-SGA) screening tool which reflexed to a formal nutrition referral for scores ≥4. Patients diagnosed with OCC, seen in our multidisciplinary clinic, and completing intent-to-cure surgery with or without adjuvant therapy were included. Data abstracted for comparison included weight, height, nutrition referral and completion, demographics, tumor characteristics, and 30-day postoperative outcomes. RESULTS: 73 patients were included in the study (35 pre-intervention and 38 post-intervention). Baseline characteristics, tumor characteristics, and surgery types were similar between groups. Following nutritional screening intervention, 30 patients (78.9%) received the pre-operative PG-SGA assessment and 70.0% scored ≥4 (required intervention) and 46.7% scored ≥9 (in critical need for intervention). Preoperative nutrition consult orders increased from 2.9% pre-intervention to 45.9% post-intervention (p < 0.001) and completed nutrition consults increased from 2.9% to 24.3% (p = 0.008). Completion of nutrition consultation was not associated with a delay to surgery. item.title: The CGRP-nociceptor axis in cancer: tumor-specific programs of immune evasion, stromal remodeling, and tumor growth.
item.dc:creator: Hua Y, Liu Y, Wang B, Liu Y, Tian X, Liu F, Tian Q, Yin F
item.description:
Authors: Hua Y, Liu Y, Wang B, Liu Y, Tian X, Liu F, Tian Q, Yin F
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1968354
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42840415



Abstract:
Cancer neuroscience has established that peripheral nerves can shape tumor growth and antitumor immunity, although the underlying mechanisms vary across malignancies. Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), released mainly by peptidergic nociceptors and sensed through the CALCRL/RAMP1 receptor complex, is emerging as a recurrent mediator of tumor-nerve communication. This review synthesizes current evidence for CGRP signaling across tumor types. In melanoma and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), CGRP can directly suppress tumor-infiltrating T cell activity. In lung adenocarcinoma, it acts through a macrophage-fibroblast relay that limits tertiary lymphoid structure assembly. In medullary thyroid cancer, tumor-associated CGRP is linked to abnormal dendritic cell development. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, nociceptor-derived CGRP participates in a reciprocal interaction with cancer-associated fibroblasts that lowers IL-15 and suppresses natural killer cells. Additional studies identify tumor-intrinsic outputs, including gastric tumor growth, CGRP-dependent cytoprotective autophagy in oral cancer, and RAMP1-dependent growth in gastrointestinal cancer models. Liver data currently support a role in fibrogenesis, while the relevance of this pathway to hepatocellular carcinoma remains unresolved. Together, these findings support a shared nociceptor-CGRP signaling system with tumor-specific cellular outputs. CGRP-pathway drugs and nociceptor-directed interventions therefore warrant tumor-specific translational studies, although anticancer efficacy remains predominantly preclinical.

item.title: Menstrual, reproductive, and contraceptive factors associated with cervical cancer in women aged ≤35 years: an individually matched case-control study.

Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to investigate the associations of menstrual, reproductive, and contraceptive characteristics with early-onset cervical cancer among women aged ≤35 years. METHODS: A hospital-based, individually matched case-control study was conducted at West China Second University Hospital from January 2022 to December 2024. A total of 300 women aged ≤35 years and with histologically confirmed cervical cancer were individually matched 1:1 to 300 screening controls within 0.5 years of age and 7 days of recruitment. Menstrual, reproductive, and contraceptive histories accrued up to 90 days before the index data were collected through standardized interviews and medical record reviews. Separate exposure-specific conditional logistic regression models stratified by matched pair were adjusted for prespecified sociodemographic, behavioral, screening-related, infection-related, and current high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) covariates. The model samples ranged from 189 to 277 matched pairs. Exploratory subgroup analyses assessed effect modification. RESULTS: In the fully adjusted model, menstrual period duration was associated with early-onset cervical cancer, with evidence of nonlinearity (P for nonlinearity <0.001). Each 1-year increase in age at first pregnancy was associated with lower odds (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.717; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.561-0.917). Higher odds were associated with greater gravidity (aOR per pregnancy, 2.959; 95% CI, 1.734-5.050), greater parity (aOR per birth, 3.667; 95% CI, 1.886-7.133), and more induced abortions (aOR per event, 2.672; 95% CI, 1.236-5.773). Longer total breastfeeding duration was inversely associated (aOR per 12 months, 0.189; 95% CI, 0.064-0.560), whereas longer cumulative combined oral contraceptive use was positively associated (aOR per 12 months, 1.335; 95% CI, 1.062-1.678). Age at menarche, menstrual cycle irregularity, ever breastfeeding, categorical combined oral contraceptive status, and other contraceptive methods were not statistically significant after full adjustment. No interaction remained statistically significant after false discovery rate correction. CONCLUSIONS: Selected menstrual, reproductive, and contraceptive characteristics were associated with early-onset cervical cancer after adjustment for measured confounders and current hrHPV status.

item.title: Clinical characteristics and immunotherapy in Chinese patients with Merkel cell carcinoma: a retrospective analysis.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare but highly aggressive cutaneous malignancy with limited epidemiological and therapeutic data in Asian populations. While immunotherapy works in Western patients, its efficacy in Chinese MCC patients remains unexplored. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 40 histologically confirmed MCC cases treated at our institution between November 2011 to November 2024. Sixteen patients with complete records underwent detailed analysis of demographics, treatments, and responses. RESULTS: The cohort included 25 female and 15 male patients (median age 71 years, range 25-91). Of the 16 patients with detailed information, 15 (94%) patients underwent extensive resection while 1 did not. Among surgical patients, 1 (7%) patient operative area received postoperative adjuvant radiotherapy, and 2 (13%) had additional lymph node dissection. Immunohistochemical analysis showed that out of 10 evaluable patients, 8 (80%) were MCPyV positive and 3 (30%) were PD-L1 positive. Among the patients receiving systemic treatment, four were administered Pembrolizumab at a dose of 200 mg every three weeks. Remarkably, three of these patients (75%) achieved a complete response (CR) by radiographic evaluation, with two of the treated specimens showed no residual malignant cells detected in post-treatment biopsy specimens. The treatment was well-tolerated, with no grade 3 or higher adverse events reported during the observation period. CONCLUSION: This study describes MCC characteristics in Chinese patients, with preliminary indications of female predominance and favorable immunotherapy responses. The findings highlight the need for standardized treatment approaches.

item.title: Reduced Nectin-4 expression in lymph node metastases of penile squamous cell carcinoma: a paired primary-metastatic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Ma T, Wang K, Chen F, Zhao H, Yang C, Wu B, Yao X
item.description:
Authors: Ma T, Wang K, Chen F, Zhao H, Yang C, Wu B, Yao X
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1912533
Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate Nectin-4 expression in primary and matched metastatic penile squamous cell carcinoma (PSCC) lesions and to assess its associations with clinicopathological features and survival outcomes. METHODS: We analyzed 123 patients with pathologically confirmed PSCC treated at our hospital between 2018 and 2024. Nectin-4 expression was assessed by immunohistochemistry using the H-score (0-300) in primary tumors and 30 matched lymph node metastases, and associations with pathological features, paired primary-metastatic differences, and survival outcomes were analyzed. RESULTS: Nectin-4 was widely expressed in PSCC. Higher Nectin-4 expression was observed in less aggressive tumors. Expression was higher in T1 than in T2 stage (95% CI 19.10-79.28; P < 0.01) and decreased from G1 to G3, with significant differences between G1 and G2 (95% CI 0.39-63.83; P = 0.047) and between G1 and G3 (95% CI 24.41-170.43; P = 0.009). Expression in primary tumors was not significantly associated with nodal status. In paired samples, lymph node metastases showed lower H-scores than their matched primary tumors (95% CI 3.52-72.82; P = 0.032). Low Nectin-4 expression was associated with shorter overall survival in Kaplan-Meier and univariable Cox analyses, but it was not independently associated with survival after multivariable adjustment. CONCLUSIONS: Nectin-4 expression in PSCC is higher in early, better-differentiated tumors and lower in lymph node metastases. Low Nectin-4 expression was associated with poorer overall survival, although it was not an independent prognostic factor. These findings suggest that Nectin-4 may have prognostic relevance and potential value as a therapeutic target in PSCC.

item.title: Subclinical pulmonary embolism in first-line/induction therapy of lung cancer - a remaining clinically relevant adverse event.
item.dc:creator: Mersmann K, Metzenmacher M, Zaun G, Wiesweg M, Oezkan F, Winantea J, Taube C, Theegarten D, Schuler M, Umutlu L, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Mersmann K, Metzenmacher M, Zaun G, Wiesweg M, Oezkan F, Winantea J, Taube C, Theegarten D, Schuler M, Umutlu L, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1886848
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42835926



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary embolism (PE) at initial diagnosis and during first-line systemic treatment is clinically relevant in patients with lung cancer. However, real-world incidence of subclinical PE is not well established. METHODS: Retrospective single-center analysis of patients at least 18 years old with non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) or small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) who received first-line/induction systemic therapy. All patients underwent contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) of the thorax with bolus tracking for PE detection. Treatment response was assessed by restaging at weeks 6 and 12 after treatment initiation. RESULTS: A total of 373 patients treated between 2019 and 2022 were included (261 NSCLC, 112 SCLC; 179 women and 194 men; median age 66 years [range, 22 to 86]; median smoking history 40 Pack Years [range, 0-150]). There was a predominance of locally advanced and metastatic disease (IB-IIB, n = 22; IIIA-C, n = 123; IVA-B, n = 228). Adenocarcinoma was the predominant histology among NSCLC cases (LUAD, n = 146), followed by squamous cell carcinoma and other NSCLC subtypes combined (n = 115); 112 patients had SCLC.PE was detected in 61/373 patients, of whom 58 (95%) had subclinical PE. In NSCLC, body-mass-index (BMI) was independently associated with occurrence of PE (OR = 1.111, p = 0.005), while central tumor localization (OR 5.637, p = 0.028) and vascular infiltration (OR 7.683, p = 0.010) were significantly associated with PE in SCLC. All patients with PE received anticoagulants according to national and international guidelines and no PE-related deaths occurred. CONCLUSION: This single-center analysis demonstrates a high incidence of subclinical PE in newly diagnosed lung cancer patients and identifies clinical risk factors associated with PE development.

item.title: The tongue may not move, but the voice will: preoperative AI voice cloning for identity preservation in major glossectomy - a prospective feasibility study.
item.dc:creator: Dange PS, Rao KN, Tv K, Shetty T, Kapahtia R, Chaitanya K, Mp S
item.description:
Authors: Dange PS, Rao KN, Tv K, Shetty T, Kapahtia R, Chaitanya K, Mp S
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1915964
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42835110



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major glossectomy frequently results in profound speech impairment. We investigated whether a patient's voice could be captured preoperatively and reconstructed using artificial intelligence voice cloning for potential future use as a personalized assistive communication voice during postoperative recovery. METHODS: In this prospective single-centre feasibility study, adult patients with treatment-naïve carcinoma of the tongue planned for major glossectomy underwent a single approximately 30-60 second preoperative voice recording in a sound-treated room. Voices were cloned offline using the IndicF5 flow-matching text-to-speech model, generating a standardized reading-passage output and a patient-transcript output for each participant. Speaker fidelity was assessed using cosine similarity across three independent speaker-verification encoders, calibrated against each patient's intra-speaker and cohort impostor distributions, alongside mel-cepstral distortion and prosodic feature analysis. Subjective acceptance was assessed using the Personalised Synthetic Voice Acceptance Questionnaire across six domains, completed by patients and family members. RESULTS: Of 34 enrolled patients, 26 formed the final cohort across four languages. Mean cosine similarity was 0.933 (Resemblyzer), 0.969 (WavLM), and 0.806 (ECAPA-TDNN), with clone scores generally falling within patient-specific intra-speaker distributions and above cohort impostor distributions. Mean mel-cepstral distortion was 7.87 dB. Fundamental frequency and other prosodic measures showed broad cohort-level correspondence with variable individual deviations. Identity-and-Ownership and Authenticity-and-Trust domains scored highest among both patients and family or attenders, while naturalness and emotional acceptance were rated more conservatively. CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate the feasibility of generating personalised synthetic voices from brief preoperative clinic-grade recordings, with objective speaker similarity and preliminary patient- and family-reported acceptance. The findings support further evaluation of these voices as potential assistive communication tools during postoperative recovery; however, postoperative communication performance and clinical benefit were not evaluated in the present study.

item.title: Percutaneous microwave ablation of hyperfunctioning parathyroid lesions under multiparametric ultrasound guidance for primary hyperparathyroidism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Lum MK, Wang J, Ye Z, Wu B, Vetshev FP, Vetsheva NN, Baek JH, Saliba MB
item.description:
Authors: Lum MK, Wang J, Ye Z, Wu B, Vetshev FP, Vetsheva NN, Baek JH, Saliba MB
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1921204
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42835108



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiparametric ultrasound (MPUS)-guided percutaneous microwave ablation (MWA) has emerged as a minimally invasive treatment option for primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT), but pooled evidence on longitudinal biochemical outcomes and safety remains limited. OBJECTIVE: This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of percutaneous MWA performed under ultrasound guidance for PHPT. METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, eligible cohort studies were retrieved from five electronic databases. Pooled cure rates, serial changes in intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH), serum calcium and phosphorus, overall complication rates, and adenoma volume reduction were calculated via random-effects models. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the robustness of the pooled estimates. RESULTS: Nine cohorts enrolling 355 PHPT patients were included. Technical success was 100%. Pooled clinical cure rates reached 86.0% at 6 months, 82.0% at 12 months, and 75.0% at the last available follow-up. Serum calcium and iPTH declined significantly, and serum phosphorus rose across all time points. The pooled patient-level overall complication rate was 11.0%, with transient hoarseness and transient hypocalcemia being the most commonly reported event-specific complications, whereas permanent recurrent laryngeal nerve injury was rare. CONCLUSION: Current evidence suggests that percutaneous MWA performed under ultrasound guidance may be a minimally invasive treatment option for appropriately selected patients with PHPT, providing acceptable mid-term biochemical improvement with a tolerable safety profile.
